idiom_name: macro instantiation (X-macro style) + C11 _Generic; hand-written vtable struct when runtime dispatch is needed
implementation_notes: C has neither class templates nor inheritance, so a base cannot be parameterized on the type that derives from it; the static-polymorphism goal is met instead by macros that emit a complete set of type-specific functions per instantiation (X-macro style, e.g. DEFINE_VECTOR(int)) and by C11 _Generic, which selects an expression at compile time from the type of a controlling expression - the standard itself uses this for <tgmath.h>. When the type must be chosen at runtime, the C idiom is a vtable struct of function pointers initialized per type, i.e. explicit dynamic dispatch. Choose between macro instantiation (compile-time, no indirection) and vtable structs (runtime, indirect); CRTP-style self-reference is not expressible.
pitfalls: Macro instantiation gives no useful checking of the emitted code until it is used: errors surface at the instantiation site, and every instantiation is a separate copy to compile and debug.

_Generic matches the type after lvalue conversion only - qualified types, arrays and function designators select differently than expected - and without a default association an unmatched type is a compile error.
A vtable struct needs one initialized function pointer per operation: a missed field is an unchecked null-pointer call at runtime.
alternative: Macro-generated per-type code (X-macro/parametric macros) plus C11 _Generic for compile-time type selection; where the type is only known at runtime, a hand-written vtable struct of function pointers initialized per type.
